keyFindings.description: The second-order-install rule this round added contradicts itself, and its worked example points a role at the container's ephemeral filesystem. It sanctions an install when (1) 'what it writes lands under the issue's own volume through the documented variables' and (2) nothing else resolves differently afterwards — then two sentences later says 'a second toolchain under `$HOME` that only an explicit absolute path reaches is sanctioned', and closes with 'a sanctioned install is paid once per issue, on the issue's own disk, by the issue's roles together'. `$HOME` is not on the issue's volume. Measured in this live role container: `df` puts /home/legion on the container root (`none 8.0E /`) while /legion is the 49 GiB issue volume (`none 49G 5.2G used`); `podHome = "/home/legion"` at packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/names.go:84 with no VolumeMount there, and `roleEnvironment` (manifest.go:728-739) relocates XDG_*, TMPDIR, GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE, BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, UV_CACHE_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR but never $HOME itself. So the example fails the rule's own first condition, the install is per role per pod rather than once per issue, and a worker who obeys it lands a toolchain on the filesystem whose eviction is exactly what manifest.go:703-709 moved the caches off. Two further clauses in the same paragraph: 'a browser download under a relocated browsers path passes both' names a configuration the role environment does not provide (no PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR or any browsers path anywhere under packages/daemon/internal/runtime/), and 'the documented variables' is not a set a worker can identify — tools.md:61-65 and :83 name five, docs/kubernetes.md:189 names a different seven, and neither list carries that label. And this paragraph replaced an explicit escalation ('Treat that as unsettled and ask the architect that owns your issue'), which no finding of rounds 1-3 asked to be settled and which this round's own implement handoff still describes as unsettled and sent to the architect — the handoff contradicts the diff. Same text at docs/kubernetes.md:226-236 and in the committed bundle.

`sqlite3`'s stated reason is false in both session stores Legion runs, and it is the recorded justification for a package this change puts behind a hard boot gate. 'Oh My Pi's own session files are SQLite databases, and a role reading its own session or a repository's SQLite fixture has no other way to open one.' Measured in this role container: the session is a JSONL tree — $XDG_STATE_HOME/dispatch/sessions/<id>/ holds results.jsonl, state.json and title, and no .db anywhere under it. Under the other store the pods run (docs/kubernetes.md:689, :700, :774 — OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=sql with OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE) sessions are rows in Postgres, whose client is the psql on the same apt line. A worker acting on this points sqlite3 at a directory of JSONL. What is true, and nearby: Oh My Pi's profile state is SQLite — /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/{agent,history,models,skill-descriptions}.db exist in this container — and 'a repository's SQLite fixture' stands on its own. The fix is to say that, not to drop sqlite3. Four hand-maintained copies carry the false clause: this one, docs/kubernetes.md:109-111, packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile:496-497, and the Go doc comment at packages/daemon/internal/capabilities/image.go:255.

The instruction for a tool no runner reaches names two of the five places the change actually touches, and a worker who follows it literally opens a red pull request: 'a pull request against sjawhar/legion that adds it to packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile and to the `toolchain` row in packages/daemon/internal/capabilities/image.go' (same at AGENTS.md:125). This pull request is its own counter-example — it needed image.go:261 (the onPath list), capabilities.go:96 (the row Summary), capabilitiestest/capabilitiestest.go:14 (the stub `binaries`) and image_test.go:140. The last two are not optional: InstallBinaries (capabilitiestest.go:34-42) writes a stub for every name in `binaries`, so a name added to onPath without one has no stub, the row reports missing, and both TestCheckImageRendersEveryRowWhenEveryImageRowIsPresent and TestToolchainSummaryNamesTheListToolchainChecks fail. One clause in both files: name packages/daemon/internal/capabilities as the unit, or spell out the four Go sites.

'Check this list first: each of these is on your `PATH` now, and needs no runner.' Read out of the image after the digest roll this is true, and read out of the checkout today it is false — and AGENTS.md:125, the auto-loaded root index, points a role working this repository at the checkout path. Measured in this role container on the digest the deployment pins today: `command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig` → all MISSING. This is the sentence class the issue's own architect named as the one that must not be met without its boundary: a role told 'the tools are in the pod' before the roll has been told something not yet true of any running role. The pull request body carries the boundary in its first `Not proven / risk` bullet; the skill text a role reads does not. One clause — 'once your pod runs an image at or after this change'.

Reported, not requested, and I could not drive it: 'dig -v prints its version on stderr' (same at docs/kubernetes.md:528). The thermonuclear pair read trixie's bind9 source for 1:9.20.26-1~deb13u1 — bin/dig/dig.c:2689-2691 is `printf("DiG %s\n", PACKAGE_VERSION); exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);`, stdout — with Debian's patch series touching neither. `dig` is absent on the digest this container runs, so I could not check it here; the Job the implementer already runs on this change's own image tag can, in one command. Acting on the wrong half costs a reader nothing, since the build step's `dig -v` passes either way, which is why it is reported rather than requested; it is worth the clause while the file is open. The neighbouring `nc` claim is correct.

ciRead: Base main requires lint, typecheck, test and pr-title. The branch's newest pull_request run head is the code head a13895797a2b90913d867320df504617ee319bb4; its check-runs show lint, typecheck, test and pr-title all completed/success, with Tests run 40139435136, Legion Envoy and Contracts 40139435137, Docs 40139435109, PR Title 40139435130 and Worker Image 40139435125 all success. compare a1389579...a07f0088 is `ahead` with only .legion/INFRA-221/implement.json and test.json, so those checks stand for the code under review. GitHub reports the pull request MERGEABLE.
threads: Twenty threads, all of rounds 1 to 3, each carrying the implementer's disposition and resolved by it. I read all five of this round's resolutions against the tree and accept them, and unresolved none. This round's four findings and one report are new threads.
acceptedThisRound: AGENTS.md:125 now gives `uvx --from <package>@<version> <command>` and names `uv run --with <package>==<version>` for a library; the cross-reference clause to the parent's workload row is there, and main's AGENTS.md does carry that row (read from GitHub at ref main), so it resolves once this merges.
The byte-stability claim and the test resting on it are gone, replaced by a paragraph that says what a pin binds and what it does not, with the emptied-cache measurement.

The provenance passage now says provenance proves build origin and not identity, with a command that reads the attestation's subject repository. I ran the chain: it prints {"ref": "refs/heads/main", "repository": "https://github.com/biomejs/biome", "path": ".github/workflows/release.yml"}, exactly as documented.
The $HOME paragraph is now true in every clause against what a role measures.

PyYAML is routed as a library with `uv run --with pyyaml==6.0.2 --no-project`, with its own section and the reason `uvx pyyaml@6.0.2` is the wrong reach; the LEGION-748 note carries it beside shellcheck's.
verifiedMyself: $HOME is not the issue's volume: df shows /home/legion on the container root (none 8.0E) and /legion as the 49 GiB issue volume; names.go:84 podHome with no mount; roleEnvironment relocates everything but $HOME.
The session store: $XDG_STATE_HOME/dispatch/sessions/<id>/ holds results.jsonl, state.json and title and no .db; the SQLite files are /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/*.db.
The five tools are MISSING on the digest this container runs.
The provenance chain prints the biomejs/biome workflow object field for field.
main's AGENTS.md carries the 'Run a database, broker or server the work needs' row the new cross-reference names.
capabilitiestest.InstallBinaries writes a stub per name in `binaries`, so that list is required by any new toolchain name.

thermonuclear.codeQuality: CHANGES at a07f0088 — 2 blocking (sqlite3's false session justification in four copies, the image-change instruction naming two of five sites) and the duplication reported; no name or form drift across the hand-maintained lists this round.

fastFollow: Unchanged and still the one cleanup item: the runner forms, the transcripts and now the whole second-order paragraph are triplicated across docs/kubernetes.md, skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md and its generated bundle copy, with neither hand-maintained file marked derived. The mechanism, not the line count, is the argument: a prescription kept by hand in three files drifts the first time it is corrected, which was round 3's first finding, and three of this round's four findings are again one clause in two or four copies.
